title: PRD: Map postmortem action items to explicit acceptance criteria and scoped implementation plan
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Summary: Translate the June 2025 kv-cache outage postmortem action items into concrete PRD changes for the serving runtime and Redwood Console. This ticket captures the set of new acceptance criteria, a prioritized scope split (MVP vs deferred), required telemetry/runbook updates, and the rollout verification plan. Goal: ensure every postmortem action that affects product behavior or operator experience is captured as testable PRD acceptance criteria or a tracked follow-up with an owner.
motivation: The postmortem identified three classes of gaps: unclear rollback contracts, insufficient KV cache telemetry to detect stall patterns, and missing runbook steps for cross-region routing fallback. Current PRD language is high-level and does not provide verifiable gates for releases. We must avoid recurring incidents by operationalizing postmortem fixes into the product spec and release definition.
scope_changes: Add: Explicit 'cache-regeneration' rollout gate that requires KV cache stall synthetic tests to pass in staging before canary.
Add: Console dashboard panel with per-tenant KV cache stall rate and median regen latency (SLO-bound metrics).
Add: Runbook step to automatically reduce batch sizes when tail-latency exceeds threshold (MVP: config flag + telemetry; Deferred: autoscaling policy).
Defer: Auto-repair kernel swapping feature to a follow-up spike (moved out of scope for runtime-1.22).
Adjust: Release criteria now require canary traffic to run a 30m synthetic workload exercising long-tail token sequences.
Add: Safety fallback: route 10% of traffic to a lower-capacity but higher-stability model variant during cache backfills.
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: Staging environment must include a synthetic KV cache stall test that reproduces observed stall signature; results must be recorded in the release dashboard and pass within two consecutive runs before canary is enabled.
AC-02: Console adds a per-tenant 'Cache Stall' panel showing stall rate, regen latency p50/p95/p99; metrics must be available for last 24h and 7d, with alert queries documented.
AC-03: Runbook amended with a validated 'Cache Stall' play that lists detection query, initial mitigation steps, and escalation path; play must be reviewed and signed-off by SRE and Product Ops.
AC-04: An automated test in CI that exercises a fallback routing policy and asserts that requests are served (no 5xx) with bounded error rate when primary model pool is degraded.
AC-05: Deployment checklist includes a 'kv-cache synthetic pass' checkbox; release is blocked if not completed.

notes: Trade-offs: Immediate full auto-repair (kernel swap) was deprioritized due to risk and time; instead we implement conservative fallback routing and stronger telemetry to enable safe future automation.
Rollout plan: gated canary -> 10% traffic fallback -> full rollout. Each step requires synthetic test pass and operator sign-off.
Operator training: schedule 1-hour runbook run-through with Customer Ops before runtime-1.22 freeze.
